title: Why I talk about programming and what you can get from it
summary: NH explains why he discusses programming concepts rather than handing out templates: natural lifters should learn to program for themselves, which frees them from people selling cookie-cutter programs. He makes an exception for novices, who need a written program as a crutch until they gain confidence. He wants viewers to think independently, not become clones who treat his words as gospel.

claims.claim: Being able to program for yourself is critical for natural lifters, bodybuilders or powerlifters alike.
Programming knowledge comes mostly from your own study and accumulated lifting experience, not from books, YouTube or being told what to do.
He has never followed anyone else's program; he learned by gathering information and doing his own thing.
Knowing how to program frees you to build the body you want and protects you from people trying to take advantage of you.
Selling the same pre-made template to a hundred people is insulting; charging for a truly individual program is understandable.
He blames buyers of pre-made programs more than sellers; even novices should have a spirit of exploration in programming, unlike form, which requires following a procedure.
Novices are the exception: they are the most numerous, often uncomfortable in the gym, and need a written program to hold on to until they gain confidence and can emancipate themselves.

He explains the reasoning behind each programming choice (e.g., deficit deadlifts for range of motion and leg drive, placed where recovery and synergy fit) so viewers learn transferable keys rather than orders.
His philosophy: he won't sell you a fish, and won't even dictate how to fish, but will explain the broader concept so you can choose your own method.
He doesn't want to create an army of clones who treat his words as gospel or idolize him; blindly following someone stunts your growth as a lifter.
The goal is to develop an eye for BS so you can immediately spot when something looks strange and be skeptical.
